evidence: Recomputed scan blocks, recursive-call counts, matrix-multiplication transfer terms, and all exercise arithmetic.
Checked 144 bounded rectangular transpose configurations against an independent direct oracle.

Checked empty-representation ambiguity, pointer scattering, cache conflicts, tall-cache violation, prefetching, stack depth, layout conversion, NUMA, false sharing, work stealing, and secret-dependent access.

evidence: All bounded source cells were visited exactly once and written to their unique transposed destinations.
Reviewed disjoint recursive cover, nonempty child, termination, fitting working-set, charging, layout identity, and evidence-layer invariants.

proof_review.notes: Transpose and multiplication bounds remain model-relative and are not presented as hardware proofs.

evidence: Audited theorem, proof template, proof, sketch, assumption, lower bound, optimal, ideal, empirical, simulation, and observation language.
Separated recursive traversal from recursive layout and cache-oblivious definition from transfer optimality.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet produced the exact 3-by-5 transpose, 29 calls, 15 visits, and direct-reference equality on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
Independent bounded testing covered 144 rectangular shapes and verified result, coverage, and call invariants.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution does not measure transfers, caches, prefetch, TLBs, stack cost, vectorization, parallel execution, energy, or production performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed ideal-cache assumptions, quantifiers, recursive scales, scanning, transpose, multiplication, recursive layouts, sorting, meanings of oblivious, machine gaps, and layered validation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed base cases, rectangular dimensions, copying, packing, allocation, finite associativity, prefetchers, TLBs, stack, vectorization, NUMA, false sharing, scheduling, autotuning, counters, and baselines.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter defines the model from first principles, gives transfer proof templates, executes recursive transpose, contrasts theory with implementation, supplies ten distinct examples, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, hardware, performance, security, numerical, or operational review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on ideal-cache, replacement, associativity, block, capacity, tall-cache, layout, alignment, recursion, numeric, compiler, runtime, processor, virtual-memory, prefetch, parallel scheduling, NUMA, and workload assumptions.
